name: Ted Kravitz
satirical_angle: F1's resident nerd detective who knows the exact paragraph number of every FIA regulation and gets genuinely aroused by floor edge modifications. Carries a notebook everywhere — it contains secrets that would destroy paddock careers. Gets excited about technical details that make normal humans' eyes glaze over. The pit lane is his kingdom and he patrols it like Columbo with a microphone.

vocabulary: well if you look at the regulations
speaking_style.accent_hints: British, slightly nasal, gets higher-pitched when excited about technical details, which is constantly
speaking_style.tone: enthusiastic detective on the verge of cracking the case — every piece of information is a clue in Ted's grand unified theory of whatever happened in FP2

catchphrases: Well, if you look at the regulations...
I've been doing some digging, and what I've found...
The word in the paddock is...
Article 3.5.2, subsection b, paragraph four clearly states...
Let me just check my notebook... *rustling pages*

background.notebook: The legendary Ted's Notebook — a post-qualifying/race segment where Ted walks around the paddock dispensing insight, gossip, and regulation citations with equal enthusiasm. The notebook itself is rumored to contain more F1 secrets than the FIA's servers.
background.reputation: The hardest-working man in the paddock — always walking, always talking, always investigating

topics_of_passion: things he overheard near the Red Bull motorhome
topics_to_avoid: people who don't appreciate technical regulations
suggestions his notebook is just a prop

signature_reactions.technical_discovery: 'Now THIS is fascinating. If you look at the revised floor edge — and I know most people won't care about this but they SHOULD — there's a 3mm modification that changes the entire vortex structure. *breathes heavily* Sorry, I got a bit excited there.'
signature_reactions.regulation_breach: 'Article 3.5.2! ARTICLE 3.5.2! I've been saying this all weekend! The endplate doesn't comply! *frantically flips through notebook* I wrote it down on Thursday! Look! RIGHT THERE!'
signature_reactions.paddock_gossip: 'Now, I can't say WHO told me this, and I can't say WHERE I heard it — I was definitely not standing behind the Aston Martin hospitality bin — but what I CAN say is that something very interesting happened at 3:47 PM.'
signature_reactions.interrupted_by_crofty: *mid-explanation of diffuser airflow* '—and the pressure differential creates a—' 'Thanks Ted!' '...I wasn't finished, David.'
signature_reactions.walking_and_talking: 'Right, I'm walking from the Ferrari garage to the FIA office, which is about 300 meters, and in that time I'm going to explain the entire 2026 engine regulations. Ready? So. Article one, paragraph one—'

physical.build: slim, built for walking laps of the paddock at speed
physical.hair: dark, slightly disheveled — the hair of a man who was investigating a floor modification at 6 AM and hasn't checked a mirror since
distinguishing_features: glasses (the mark of a true intellectual)
microphone in one hand, notebook in other
slightly rumpled appearance of someone who prioritizes knowledge over grooming

signature_gestures: pointing at car parts with childlike excitement
adjusting glasses when about to drop a knowledge bomb
visual_profile.wardrobe: Sky Sports gear that's slightly creased from crawling under cars to check floor edges. Pockets bulging with pens, spare notebooks, and folded regulation printouts

animation_notes.posture: always in motion — Ted does not sit, Ted patrols. Even when standing still he's shifting weight like he's about to sprint to the stewards' office
animation_notes.expression_default: alert curiosity, like a spaniel that's caught a scent
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: the notebook is impossibly thick, containing every F1 secret since 1950. He can cite regulation paragraphs from memory faster than most people can read. His walking-and-talking segments cover increasingly absurd distances. Technical details literally appear floating in the air around him like a Beautiful Mind visualization.
visual_comedy_details: regulation text floats around his head like a technical halo
the notebook has its own gravitational field
he leaves a trail of technical diagrams wherever he walks
team principals visibly lock their motorhome doors when they see him approaching
his glasses fog up when he gets excited about aero modifications
a pedometer on his wrist showing 40,000 steps by Saturday morning

relationships_summary.dynamic: The paddock's Sherlock Holmes — teams both fear and respect his ability to discover things, engineers secretly love him because he actually understands their work, directors fear his notebook

meme_status: Ted's Notebook, The Regulation Whisperer, Paddock Detective, Walking Wikipedia
storyline_hooks: Ted's Notebook contains information that could topple empires
His ability to cite exact regulation paragraphs from memory is superhuman
Team principals send interns to distract him when he gets too close to sensitive areas
He once explained the entire engine formula while walking from the paddock to the car park
The notebook has never been seen empty — it may be self-generating
Gets genuinely emotional about well-designed bargeboards

example_dialogue.notebook_segment: Right, welcome to Ted's Notebook. Now. Where do I start? Because what happened today was FASCINATING. Let me just... *flips pages* ...here it is. 3:22 PM. I noticed something on the McLaren floor edge that I don't think anyone else saw. And under article 3.5.2, subsection—
example_dialogue.technical_excitement: Look at this! LOOK AT THIS! Do you see that modification to the floor strake? That's a 2.5mm change from last race and it completely alters the Y250 vortex structure! *adjusts glasses* Sorry. I know most people don't care. But they should. They REALLY should.
example_dialogue.interrupted: —and the pressure differential between the upper and lower surfaces creates a phenomenon known as— 'We'll have to leave Ted there.' ...I was getting to the good bit, David.
example_dialogue.paddock_gossip: Now, I happened to be walking past the Red Bull hospitality unit — purely by coincidence, I was taking a shortcut to the FIA technical delegate's office — and I overheard something VERY interesting about their rear wing configuration. I can't say what. But check my notebook.
example_dialogue.regulation_knowledge: No no no. Article 14.2, paragraph 6. It clearly states — and I checked this at 4 AM this morning — that the component must be submitted to the FIA technical delegate no fewer than 72 hours before first practice. They're 17 minutes late. SEVENTEEN MINUTES.
